name: Creamy Korean Pumpkin Porridge (Hobakjuk)
why: Hobakjuk is the dish Koreans turn to as autumn deepens — silky, naturally sweet kabocha porridge that's perfect for these first cold October mornings. A Korean technique that's genuinely new territory, and it comes together in 35 minutes with just a few ingredients.
author: Henry
ingredients: 1.5 lb (670 g) kabocha pumpkin (or other deep-orange-fleshed pumpkin), peeled, seeded and chunked
2/3 cup (160 ml) Korean sweet rice (chapssal) — or regular round-grain white rice
3-4 tbsp (37-50 g) white sugar, to taste
1-2 tbsp (20-40 ml) honey (or light brown sugar)
1 tbsp (10 g) toasted pine nuts, to garnish (optional)

steps: Rinse the sweet rice several times until the water runs mostly clear, then soak in cold water for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel the kabocha, scoop out the seeds, and cut the flesh into large chunks (roughly 3-4 cm).
Place the pumpkin chunks and drained rice in a large pot and add 4 cups (1 liter) of water.
Cover and bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to a steady simmer.
Simmer for about 15 minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking, until the pumpkin breaks apart easily and the rice is completely tender.
Turn off the heat and puree everything with an immersion blender until completely smooth (or blend in batches in a countertop blender, letting the hot liquid cool slightly first).
If the porridge is too thick, thin with a splash of hot water until it's pourable but still creamy.
Stir in the sugar, honey and a pinch of salt. Taste and adjust the sweetness to your liking — kabocha is naturally sweet, so build up gradually.
Ladle into bowls while hot and garnish with toasted pine nuts.
Serve immediately — it's great for breakfast, dessert, or a late-night bowl.

pro_tips: Kabocha is in its prime right now and is far sweeter than butternut — if you only have butternut, bump the sugar to 4 tbsp and add a pinch more salt.
Toasting the pine nuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes before sprinkling on top adds a serious lift. Swap for chopped walnuts if you can't find pine nuts.
